question_text: Define bond enthalpy. Give an example.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: Bond enthalpy: the enthalpy change when
one mole of bonds of a given type is
broken, with all species in the gaseous
Breaking a bond absorbs energy, so bond
steps.why: A bond holds two atoms together, so pulling them apart needs energy from outside — bond breaking is endothermic by definition.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the gaseous state — in a liquid or solid, other interactions mix into the value.
Writing a negative bond enthalpy. Breaking absorbs; forming releases.
steps.memory_tip: Breaking costs energy, forming returns it — bond enthalpy is the breaking side, so it is positive.
steps.margin_note: One mole of bonds, gaseous state, positive sign.

steps.label: The example
lines: In molecules with several equal bonds,
such as CH₄, the mean (average) bond
steps.why: H₂ is the cleanest example because it has exactly one bond. In CH₄ the four C−H bonds break one after another with different values, so their average is quoted.
common_mistakes: Using a solid or a solution in the example equation — every species must be gaseous.
steps.memory_tip: H₂ to 2H costs about 436 kJ per mole — one bond, one clean number.
steps.margin_note: The mean-bond-enthalpy line covers the polyatomic case.

insider_note: Definition and example, one mark each, and the example fails if any species in it is not gaseous. H₂ is the safest choice because it has exactly one bond and so needs no mean value.
